title: 10 Year Natural Transformation 15-25 (from 110 to 210 lbs)
summary: 1000-subscriber special walking through photos from age 15 to 25: from a 110 lb high-schooler doing knee push-ups, to 6 ft 140 lb at 18, through bedroom dumbbell training with daily biceps, to gym training, a clean bulk to 210 lb, then an over-aggressive bulk to 235 lb at ~21-22% bodyfat and a crash cut. He uses it to argue that bad genetics and so-called natural limits shouldn't stop anyone, that natural progress takes patience, and that reckless bulking is a trap.

claims.claim: At 15 he weighed 110 lb, was the smallest in his class, and decided he didn't want to be small for the rest of his life; that is what made him start training.
When he started he couldn't do a single push-up; three or four knee push-ups wiped him out and he could only work out for about 10 minutes.
He grew almost a foot in three years during puberty while his weight barely rose, leaving him with arms of maybe 10-11 inches; he was training against his body's growth.
From 15 he trained daily with push-ups, sit-ups, squats and curling chairs, and ate like a madman.
At 18 he was 6 ft and about 140 lb, still with spaghetti arms and no legs; only his neck grew thick through puberty without training, which he credits to genetics.
At 18 he bought dumbbells and trained in his bedroom every day, partly because he started playing football against 180-190 lb players who smashed him.
Early on he curled maybe 15 lb dumbbells and trained biceps every single day because he desperately wanted big arms.
He only really started gaining weight once he began lifting and eating more; skinny guys must eat when they train or it's all for nothing.
His traps grew without direct work, just from doing lots of rows.
At 19, after about four years of training, he weighed around 150-160 lb and still looked untrained; building a physique naturally is a game of patience.
After almost a year of daily rows his back still showed no lats or erectors; with bottom-of-the-barrel genetics progress is slow, but that same area is now packed with muscle.
Judging your body when you just start and deciding you can't grow because of genetics is nonsense; you don't know your full potential.
At 20, after close to three years of daily dumbbell biceps work, his biceps were overdeveloped relative to the rest of his arm: what grew was what he trained.
At 20 people told him he had reached his natural limit as an ectomorph at 170 lb and 6 ft and should stop wasting his time.
At 21 he was around 185-190 lb and decided to bulk.
At 22 during a hard bulk he was 200-205 lb; gaining some fat is fine and expected when bulking, and it helps you look bigger, but you don't need to get super fat.
He played football and basketball before falling in love with weight training, then moved from home training to a real gym doing bench, squat and deadlift.
At the end of his clean bulk he was 210 lb, after seven to eight years of training; someone with better genetics would need much less time to get there.
He then bulked aggressively to 225, 230 and finally 235 lb at 6 ft, too obsessed with size, eating too much and not training smart, so his physique got sloppy.
Skinny guys are likely to fall into the trap of trying to get too big too fast; muscle builds slowly while fat builds fast, so be patient.
At his heaviest he estimates he was about 21-22% bodyfat, which is way too high and unnecessary for natural bodybuilding.
When his health started to suffer he did a crash cut; he advises against crash cuts because they are dangerous for health, cost strength, feel bad mentally and can lose muscle.
If you gained too much too fast, the fix is patience, not a crash cut; over time you can build a lean, massive physique naturally.
There is no such thing as a natural limit; the only limit is the one you impose on yourself.
At every stage (15, 17, 20, 21) the same people told him he had hit his limit, first that he was too small, then that his growth looked unnatural; at 210 lb and 6 ft he is still improving.
His channel's mission is to promote natural bodybuilding and give the advice he wished he had when starting.

exercises.why: trained daily for years; biceps became his most developed part

exercises.why: done daily; grew his traps indirectly
